title: Exactness of coordinate induced maps on inverse limits
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $F,G,H$ be towers of $R$-modules indexed by $\mathbf N$. Let $\alpha_n:F_n\to G_n$ and $\beta_n:G_n\to H_n$ commute with successor transition maps, with $0\to F_n\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}G_n\xrightarrow{\beta_n}H_n\to0$ exact at every index. Let $U:\varprojlim F\to\varprojlim G$ and $V:\varprojlim G\to\varprojlim H$ be linear maps characterized by these coordinate maps. Then $U$ is injective and $\operatorname{im}U=\ker V$. If every successor transition in $F$ is surjective, then $V$ is surjective.

proof.text: A successor-compatible family is a section: induction on n ≤ m proves compatibility with every transition. The forgetful functor from modules preserves limits, and Mathlib Types.isLimitEquivSections realizes each such section as a unique limit element.
If U(x)=U(y), each coordinate of x and y agrees by coordinate injectivity of alpha; concrete limit extensionality gives x=y.

For y in ker V, exactness gives a preimage x_n under alpha_n at each coordinate. Naturality of alpha and its injectivity force transition(x_(n+1))=x_n. Realize this family in lim F. Its U-image is y by coordinates. Conversely beta_n(alpha_n(x_n))=0 coordinatewise proves V(U(x))=0.

Fix z in lim H. Given b_n lifting z_n, choose b_prime lifting z_(n+1). By naturality of beta the defect transition(b_prime)-b_n is in ker beta_n. Write it as alpha_n(a), lift a along the surjective F transition to a_prime, and replace b_prime by b_prime-alpha_(n+1)(a_prime). This preserves its beta-image and makes its transition b_n. Recursively choose such corrected lifts, realize their compatible family in lim G, and verify its V-image equals z by coordinate extensionality.

proof_origin.place: Algebra Lemmas 03CA and 0598, surjective-kernel specialization; Homology Lemma 02N1(1)

lean.statement: theorem tower_limit_exact_of_coordinate_maps (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R) (G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} R) (H : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{t} R) (α : ∀ n : ℕ, F.obj (Opposite.op n) →ₗ[R] G.obj (Opposite.op n)) (β : ∀ n : ℕ, G.obj (Opposite.op n) →ₗ[R] H.obj (Opposite.op n)) (hα : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : F.obj (Opposite.op (n + 1))), G.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op (α (n + 1) x) = α n (F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op x)) (hβ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : G.obj (Opposite.op (n + 1))), H.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op (β (n + 1) x) = β n (G.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op x)) (hshort : ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Injective (α n) ∧ Function.Exact (α n) (β n) ∧ Function.Surjective (β n)) (U : ↑(limit F) →ₗ[R] ↑(limit G)) (V : ↑(limit G) →ₗ[R] ↑(limit H)) (hU : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ↑(limit F)), limit.π G (Opposite.op n) (U x) = α n (limit.π F (Opposite.op n) x)) (hV : ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ↑(limit G)), limit.π H (Opposite.op n) (V x) = β n (limit.π G (Opposite.op n) x)) : Function.Injective U ∧ Function.Exact U V ∧ ((∀ n : ℕ, Function.Surjective (F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_right n 1)).op)) → Function.Surjective V)

statement_change.old_statement: For coordinatewise short exact sequences of towers, induced maps on inverse limits are injective and exact in the middle; if the kernel tower has surjective transitions, the induced map on quotients is surjective.
statement_change.what: The Lean signature lacked transition compatibility of the coordinate maps, although the cited source requires maps of short exact sequences. Without it the surjectivity conclusion is false: F is the zero tower, G has Z at every level with zero strict transitions, H is the constant Z tower, alpha=0 and beta=id. lim G=0, lim H=Z, U=V=0 satisfy the coordinate identities, and F transitions are surjective, but V is not. Add hα and hβ, which the sole caller already assumes. This restores the source statement, not an extra restriction on the intended theorem.

citers.note: Its theorem already assumes hα and hβ. Only the call must pass these existing hypotheses; its statement is unchanged.

old_proof.text: Use injectivity and exactness in each coordinate, uniqueness of coordinate preimages, and recursive correction of lifts using surjective kernel transitions.
